issues.legal_issue: A compromise in an ejectment suit that continues the occupants as lessees on the original lease terms creates a fresh lease rather than merely extending the time for delivery of possession.
material_facts: The compromise stated that the occupants would remain as lessees and pay rent for a specified term.
It incorporated the original lease terms for matters not otherwise covered by the compromise.
The compromise also included a direction to vacate at the end of the specified term.
issues.conclusion: The compromise created a fresh lease, incorporating the original lease terms to the extent they were not replaced by the compromise.
issues.legal_principle: Whether a compromise creates a fresh lease or merely extends time for delivery of possession depends on the parties’ intention as expressed in the compromise and the decree. The use of lessee and rent language, together with incorporation of the original lease terms, supported a fresh lease here. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied upon for this conclusion.

predicates.compromise_in_pending_ejectment_suit: The parties compromised an ejectment suit while it was pending.
predicates.parties_agreed_to_continue_lessee_status: The compromise described the occupants as continuing in the capacity of lessees.
predicates.original_lease_terms_incorporated_for_un: The compromise adopted the original lease terms for matters it did not otherwise address.

issues.definition: When an ejectment-suit compromise continues occupants as lessees and adopts the original lease terms for unaddressed matters, it creates a fresh lease.

issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree directing lessees to vacate at the end of a fixed term does not authorize ejectment execution where the compromise created a lease carrying an option to renew.
material_facts: The compromise created a fresh lease for a fixed term and incorporated the original lease terms, including the renewal option.
The decree directed the lessees to vacate at the end of that term.
Execution was sought to obtain possession after the stated term, although the lessees relied on the renewal option.
issues.conclusion: The direction to vacate was ineffective as an ejectment decree; at most, it declared the lessors’ right to eject the lessees if they failed to obtain a renewal.
issues.legal_principle: A decree’s effect depends on the agreement it embodies. Where the compromise creates a lease that gives the lessees an option to renew, a direction to vacate at the end of the initial term is not an executable ejectment direction; it is at most a declaration of a right to eject if renewal is not obtained. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied upon for this conclusion.

rule.if: execution_proceeding_on_compromise_decree and compromise_created_fresh_lease and lease_includes_renewal_option and decree_directs_vacating_at_end_of_initial_term

predicates.execution_proceeding_on_compromise_decre: A party sought execution of a decree based on a compromise in an ejectment suit.
predicates.compromise_created_fresh_lease: The compromise established a fresh lease rather than merely extending time to deliver possession.
predicates.lease_includes_renewal_option: The lease gives the lessees an option to renew.
predicates.decree_directs_vacating_at_end_of_initia: The decree directs the lessees to vacate when the initial lease term ends.

issues.definition: In execution of a compromise decree, a direction to vacate at the end of an initial term does not authorize ejectment when the compromise created a lease with a renewal option.

issues.legal_issue: Fixing a term in a fresh lease does not, by itself, exclude a renewal option incorporated from the original lease.
material_facts: The compromise fixed the period during which the occupants could remain as lessees.
It incorporated the original lease terms for matters not specifically covered by the compromise.
The original lease contained a renewal option.
issues.conclusion: The renewal option remained one of the terms of the fresh lease despite the fixed term stated in the compromise.
issues.legal_principle: A renewal option is independent of the duration fixed for the initial lease term. Incorporating the original lease terms for matters not otherwise covered therefore carries the renewal option into the fresh lease, notwithstanding the fixed term. No statutory provision or earlier case was relied upon for this conclusion.

rule.if: lease_created_by_compromise and original_lease_terms_incorporated_for_unaddressed_matters and original_lease_contains_renewal_option and initial_lease_term_fixed

predicates.lease_created_by_compromise: The parties’ compromise established a lease.
predicates.original_lease_terms_incorporated_for_un: The compromise adopted the original lease terms for matters it did not otherwise address.
predicates.original_lease_contains_renewal_option: The original lease gives the lessee an option to renew.
predicates.initial_lease_term_fixed: The compromise specifies the duration of the initial lease term.

issues.definition: A renewal option in incorporated original terms remains part of a lease created by compromise even when the initial term is fixed.

issues.legal_issue: A lessor cannot unreasonably withhold consent to renewal when the lease gives the lessee an entitlement to renew subject to the lessor’s consent.
material_facts: The original lease entitled the lessees to seek renewal subject to the lessor’s consent and consultation.
The renewal provision also conditioned the entitlement on there having been no breach of a lease condition.
The lessor’s consent was therefore required, but the provision conferred an entitlement to renewal.
issues.conclusion: The lessor could withhold consent for a material breach or another reasonable ground, but could not withhold consent capriciously or unreasonably.
issues.legal_principle: The consent requirement must be read in the context of the lessee’s stated entitlement to renewal, and a contractual term should not be treated as superfluous if it can be given a reasonable meaning. The Court also applied the stated principle under English and Indian law that consent in a covenant concerning dealings with leased property is not to be unreasonably withheld, reasoning that this applies as well to consent for renewal under an express option. No earlier case or statutory provision was relied upon.

predicates.lease_renewal_dispute: The dispute concerns whether a lessee may exercise a lease renewal option.
predicates.lease_confers_entitlement_to_renew: The lease states that the lessee is entitled to renew, subject to its stated conditions.
predicates.renewal_requires_lessor_consent: The lease makes the lessor’s consent a condition of renewal.

issues.definition: When a lease entitles the lessee to renew subject to the lessor’s consent, the lessor may refuse consent only on a reasonable ground.
